thread:
rory_newhire: hi everyone, day 2 snag. SSO to the console keeps redirecting to our idp (idp.internal.redwood) but my browser times out. wireguard looks up, i can ssh to bastion, but web SSO endpoints (10.40.1.12) are unreachable from my laptop. any tips? :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

wg-bot: WireGuard: peer=rory_newhire, latest_handshake=12s ago, allowedips=10.0.0.0/8

chao-sre: welcome! first guess: split-tunnel + DNS. can you `dig idp.internal.redwood @10.10.0.2` and `dig idp.internal.redwood` (your default)? Also `ip route` output helps.

rory_newhire: `dig` to 10.10.0.2 resolves 10.40.1.12, default dig returns 203.0.113.9. ip route shows default via 192.168.1.1, wg0 exists but no internal search domain set.

tess-idp: our idp expects the company DNS to resolve internal hostnames and the browser to access the internal IP. if your laptop resolves to the public IP (203.0.113.9) the connection will fail behind allowlists.

nick-net: quick workaround: add the company DNS as a resolver for just our domains. on mac/linux you can do: `sudo bash -c "echo 'server 10.10.0.2' > /etc/resolver/internal.redwood"` (mac) or use `systemd-resolved` split DNS config on linux. Alternatively SSH tunnel the idp port: `ssh -L 8443:10.40.1.12:443 rory@bastion.redwood.internal -N` then open https://localhost:8443 to complete SSO.

rory_newhire: ssh -L to bastion worked, I could finish sign-in and access console. thanks!

chao-sre: we'll add a short note to onboarding: if your resolver returns public IPs for internal domains, use the resolver snippet or tunnel via bastion. also filing a ticket to push split-dns config to the onboarding pack so new hires don't hit this.

tess-idp: thanks. security note: don't add public consumer IP ranges to allowlists; tunneling or DNS fix is preferred.

rory_newhire: can someone paste the mac/linux resolver snippets into the onboarding doc? saved a lot of time. :relieved:
